subject.title: [Feature]: Move away from useMultiFileAuthState for Baileys

question: Should the bundled WhatsApp plugin make SQLite canonical for all Baileys credentials and signal keys, and what migration, rollback, backup, and legacy-file deletion guarantees must protect existing linked sessions?
rationale: Repository policy and upstream guidance support replacing the file store, but selecting the permanent sensitive-state owner and its irreversible migration and retention rules requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt canonical plugin SQLite
options.body: Transactionally migrate all auth material into a plugin-owned SQLite schema, verify restart, reconnect, logout, and recovery, then remove legacy files only after successful validation.

options.title: Retain hardened multi-file state
options.body: Continue atomic-write, recovery, and performance hardening without changing the persistent data model or deleting existing files.

recommendation.title: Adopt canonical plugin SQLite
recommendation.body: Transactionally migrate all auth material into a plugin-owned SQLite schema, verify restart, reconnect, logout, and recovery, then remove legacy files only after successful validation.

likelyOwner.reason: The most substantial recent merged work on WhatsApp credential persistence and recovery is in mcaxtr's auth-stabilization change.
